title.narrative: Integrated Nutrition and Child Protection lean season Response for community resilience to Vulnerable population in Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtGrow Strong Foundation (GSF) in partnership withnbspFuture Resilience and Development Foundation (FRAD), and GRACEnbspInitiatives, is proposing a six-month humanitarian project in Gubio, Ngala, and Bama LGAs of Borno State. The project will target internally displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities who continue to face acute malnutrition and protection risks, including gender-based violence (GBV) and Child protectionnbspduring the lean season.This intervention seeks to address life-threatening levels of acute malnutrition, and child protection concernsnbspaffecting IDPs, returnees and host communities in Borno State during lean season. The proposed project aligns with the objectives of the 2025 First Standard Allocation strategy, which is "Addressing Immediate Food Insecurity in North-East Nigeria" by targeting two priority LGAs experiencing crisis and emergency food insecurity (IPC Phase 4): Bama, Gubio and Ngalanbspin Borno state.ltbrgtThis proposal follows earlier support from the NHF- 2023 Standard Allocation, 2023 Reserve Allocation, the 2024 Third Reserve Allocation, and the recent 2025 First Standard Allocation. While progress has been made, the needs remain high, especially as these LGAs are still in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis). The 2nd Standard Allocation offers an opportunity to scale up services and close gaps not fully covered by ongoing interventions.ltbrgtnbsp ltbrgt1. NutritionltbrgtThe consortium will deliver a community-based nutrition package that combines treatment and prevention. Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) will be managed through the culturally adapted Tom Brown TSFP approach, while Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) without complications will be addressed through Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP) with RUTF. Children with complications will be referred to stabilization centers supported by partners in the target LGAs. Alongside treatment, preventive actions will tackle underlying causes of malnutrition such as food insecurity, seasonal disease outbreaks, and flooding.lt/pgtltpgtChild protectionlt/pgtltpgtGrow strong foundation will build on it contextual experience and expertise of providing live saving assistance and implement this six-month emergency response project which will target 5,500 direct beneficiaries including children, adolescents, and women in high-risk Local Government Areas (LGAs) in Borno states during the 2025 lean season. The project aims to reduce protection risks through structured child protection case management, family tracing and reunification, psychosocial support (PSS), and Comprehensive case arrangementnbsp. In coordination with government and local structures, GSF will strengthen community-based protection mechanisms and ensure timely referrals using CPIMS+/Primero.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtBuilding on NHF priority for inclusion in humanitarian response, disability Inclusion and Community Empowerment will be a top priority of the response strategy, the consortium will emphasize meaningful inclusion of persons with disabilities particularly women and children by embedding inclusive practices across all intervention sectors. GSFnbspwill lead the consortium initiative ensuring other cross cutting issues like gender, AAP, PSEA and protection are mainstreamed.ltbrgt ltbrgtThe consortium will implement a robust MEAL framework, including baseline and end-line assessments, monthly supportive supervision, joint monitoring visits, bi-monthly senior-level oversight, and quarterly project review meetings. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTheory of Changeltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtIf vulnerable populations in Gubio, Ngala, and Bama have access to integrated nutrition, protection, and MHPSS services, and if these interventions are monitored in real time with adjustments made as needed,nbspthen The risks of acute malnutrition and protectionnbspwill reduce. This will contribute to improved safety, resilience, and dignity for women, children, and persons with disabilities during the lean season.ltbrgtlt/pgt
